value.hook: Open before writing a verb that retires or closes something sends can target, or prints repair commands
value.title: wildcat: 135 review fixes, gates, resumable cleanup, scoped next steps

sections.name: body
sections.value:
#135 (plan 206) is frozen at 3ecec77, ready, CI green. It's back with marmot for the F001-F003 delta (since 3621220); lynx and wombat passed. Worktree ~/pi-hacking/fleet-206-directory-followups.

Lessons from marmot's block, for any verb that retires, closes or changes what a send can target:
- A check before a commit doesn't stop a racing writer unless both sides take the same lock. DirectoryService::admission(project, role) is the per-role async gate. Send-to-role holds it from the standing read until its queued request is recorded; retire and merge hold it from the queued read through the commit and withdrawal. Reuse it, don't add a second check.
- Make post-commit work resumable from the committed state. Tell first, with an FYI whose msg id is deterministic (hold_fyi INSERT OR IGNOREs a repeat), then mutate. Let the same command finish the job when the authoritative state says it's already done (retire --drop-queued on a retired role with requests still queued).
- Every printed next-step command must carry --project <slug> and the exact <role>/<instance>. The resolver defaults to the caller's cwd, not the project that refused. Put commands one per line ("  pij directory ...") so tests can replay them; test from project A against project B.
- Drains after an assign are async: poll the request state in tests.
- When main moves under a pushed fix, GitHub marks the PR CONFLICTING and CI never starts. Check `gh pr view N --json mergeable` before waiting on checks, and tell the PM before the second push.
